title: Sections of a finite constant pro-etale sheaf as continuous functions
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $V\to X$ be an object of the small pro-etale site with its small skeleton [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Give $A$ the discrete topology (every subset is open). The constant sheaf of rings $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] has canonical ring isomorphisms
$$\theta_{X,V}:A_X(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(|V|,A),$$
where $|V|$ is the underlying Zariski space and $C(|V|,A)$ is the ring of continuous functions with pointwise operations. These isomorphisms send the image of every constant-presheaf element $a\in A$ to the constant function with value $a$. For every morphism $h:W\to V$ of objects of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and every $s\in A_X(V)$ they satisfy $\theta_{X,W}(h^*s)=\theta_{X,V}(s)\circ|h|$. No quasi-compactness, connectedness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed on $X$ or $V$.

proof.text: Define the RingCat-valued presheaf F on X_proet by F(V)=C(|V|,A), with pointwise ring operations and restriction by precomposition. Its underlying set presheaf is the restriction of Mathlib continuousMapPresheaf A. The set-valued version isSheaf_fpqcTopology_continuousMapPresheaf in the same Mathlib module as [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf] proves this is an fpqc sheaf. Since the pro-etale topology is coarser than the fpqc topology and the forgetful functor from X_proet to schemes is continuous [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], restriction gives a set sheaf on X_proet. Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget promotes this to the required ring-valued sheaf. The site construction includes the weakly etale composition and base-change facts [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, printed p. 30, continuous-function sheaf assertion; the fpqc sheaf formulation is the Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Define the map phi from the constant ring presheaf P to F by sending a to the constant function a. To prove local injectivity, evaluate equal constant functions at a point of a nonempty V; if V is empty the empty sieve covers by Scheme.ProEt.bot_mem_topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For local surjectivity of f in C(|V|,A), for every point x of V let U_x be the open fibre f^{-1}({f(x)}). It is open because A is discrete. Its inclusion followed by V to X is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], hence U_x is an object of X_proet. The family of inclusions U_x to V is jointly surjective (x belongs to U_x) and consists of open immersions, so it is a Zariski covering. Mathlib zariskiPrecoverage_le_propQCPrecoverage makes it a pro-etale covering without finiteness or quasi-compactness assumptions on V. On U_x, f equals the constant f(x), so the sieve generated by this covering lies in the image sieve of phi. Therefore phi is locally surjective. The RingCat instance of GrothendieckTopology.WEqualsLocallyBijective, using that forgetting rings preserves sheafification [lem-pe-ring-sheafification-underlying-sets], applies the local-bijection criterion [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] directly to phi. Thus its sheafification is an isomorphism. Compose this isomorphism sheafify(P) to sheafify(F) with the inverse of isoSheafify for the already-proved sheaf F to obtain e: A_X to F [def-weil-pbc-sheafification, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, printed p. 30, discrete-space assertion and constant-section normalization; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 0F6D supporting the pro-etale covering context

proof.text: Naturality of the sheafification unit gives eta_P followed by e equal to phi: rewrite eta_P followed by sheafify(phi) as phi followed by eta_F, and cancel eta_F with its inverse. Each component of e is a RingCat isomorphism, and ringCatIsoToRingEquiv gives theta_V. Applying the unit equation to a gives the normalization on constants. Applying naturality of e to h:W to V and then to s gives theta_W(h^*s)=theta_V(s) composed with |h|, since F restricts by precomposition. These are the actual sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. No hypotheses have been added, and the argument includes empty and disconnected V.

split_report.summary: Split the imported statement into three proof steps. First, the existing Mathlib fpqc sheaf of continuous functions restricts to a pro-etale sheaf and gains pointwise ring operations. Second, finite discrete fibres give a pro-etale covering by open fibres, so the constant presheaf map is locally bijective and sheafification yields the canonical isomorphism. Third, pointwise operations, constant-section normalization, and restriction naturality give the ring and pullback clauses, including empty and disconnected cases.
